heard: Earth's shadow does not cause the changing phases of the Moon. For centuries, a persistent historical myth erroneously blamed our planet for blocking the Sun entirely from our view. In physical reality, the Sun continuously illuminates exactly half of the lunar globe at all times without fail. As the Moon travels along its orbital path around our world, our observing viewpoint shifts constantly every single night. This changing perspective creates everything from a delicate crescent phase to a brilliant full moon high overhead. Earth's actual physical shadow only touches the lunar surface during rare lunar eclipses occurring roughly twice per calendar year. Earth's shadow never causes the phases.
